evidence: I18nExceptionFilterPipe is decorated with @Catch(HttpException) and implements ExceptionFilter, which is framework error handling that belongs in infrastructure.
catch() uses host.switchToHttp() and response.status().json() to adapt the error at the transport boundary.
getMessage() and translateArray() turn exception messages into i18n translations and do not evaluate any business rule.
checkIfConstraintAvailable() parses the format of a message string ('title-{json}'), which is a formatting concern.
Failures are logged through the injected winston Logger, a cross-cutting infrastructure concern.
parsedVerdict.reasoning: src/common/pipes/i18n-exception-filter.pipe.ts is declared infrastructure. It is a NestJS exception filter (@Catch(HttpException), implements ExceptionFilter). Its responsibilities are cross-cutting framework concerns: catching HTTP exceptions, reading the request language, translating error messages through I18nService, shaping the error response JSON and logging failures with winston. The layer model puts filters (src/common/filters/**) and pipes in infrastructure, so this role fits. checkIfConstraintAvailable and translateArray only parse and format messages; they do not apply domain or business rules. Assigning StatusCodesList.ValidationError to 422 responses is a mapping of error codes for the response, not a business decision. No ADR prose was given. No misplaced responsibility was found.
